cards.explanation: The answer is that His ways may be known on earth, friends. Right after the blessing ask, the song says "…that Your ways may be known on earth, Your salvation among all nations." (Psalm 67:2). The blessing isn't the finish line. The song ties it to His ways being known. Think of it like a cookie box: it's made to be passed around, not hoarded in the pantry.

The answer is all the peoples, friends! The chorus says, "Let the peoples praise You, O God; let all the peoples praise You." (Psalm 67:3). Say it twice and it sounds like the song really means it. That's a big circle of voices, and nobody's left out of the line.

The answer is justly, friends! The song says the nations can be glad "…for You judge the peoples justly and lead the nations of the earth." (Psalm 67:4). That's a real reason to sing. When the Judge is just, joy makes sense.

The answer is that He leads them, friends. The verse says, "…for You judge the peoples justly and lead the nations of the earth." (Psalm 67:4). So the nations get a Judge and a Leader. I'd follow that guide way before I'd follow my own sense of direction.

The answer is its harvest, friends! The song says, "The earth has yielded its harvest…" (Psalm 67:6). The earth gave something, and the song notices. It's the kind of moment where you look at a full table and just say thank you.
The answer is True, friends! Right after the harvest line comes "God, our God, blesses us." (Psalm 67:6). The two lines sit side by side. The song hands us the harvest and the blessing in one breath.

The answer is all the ends of the earth, friends. The last line says, "God blesses us, that all the ends of the earth shall fear Him." (Psalm 67:7). The song started with "us" asking for a blessing, and it ends with the whole earth in view. That's a big finish.
